news.headline: House Democrats Back Impeachment Resolution Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth
news.summary: House Minority Leader Hakeen Jeffries publicly declared a "hard yes" to impeaching Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The resolution is expected to be introduced this week, with Democrats supporting it and some Republicans possibly defecting after recent midterm losses. The move reflects heightened partisan tensions and debates over the secretary's conduct and national security policies. The outcome could set a precedent for impeachment proceedings against a sitting cabinet official.

news.headline: Mississippi Senate race remains too close as vote count continues
news.summary: Democratic candidate Scott Colom holds a narrow lead over incumbent Republican Senator Cindy Hyde‑Smith as Mississippi continues counting absentee and affidavit ballots. The race is historically significant as Colom could become the first Black senator from the state. Both campaigns are awaiting the certification deadline while voters and officials address pending ballot reviews. The outcome will affect Senate control and Democratic strategy in the South.

news.headline: US lawmakers summon Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over alleged Chinese spy ties
news.summary: U.S. intelligence officials warned that a woman close to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security. Republican committee chairs have sent a letter requesting Huang appear before Congress to brief them on the matter. The issue raises concerns about potential espionage and national security risks tied to a leading tech company. The White House later canceled a tech advisory panel that would have included Huang.

news.headline: Kennedy family sues to block Trump's proposed Arlington memorial arch
news.summary: Nine members of the Kennedy family have filed a lawsuit seeking to halt President Trump's plan to build a 250-foot memorial arch near Arlington National Cemetery. The filing argues the structure could obstruct views of Kennedy gravesites and cast a shadow over the historic site. The case adds to a growing legal challenge against the project as Trump prepares to attend a Veterans Day ceremony at the cemetery. The outcome could affect how memorials are approved near federal burial grounds.

news.headline: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent Relocates to Military Base Amid Iranian Threats
news.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has moved from his Washington-area home to a military base after reports of Iranian threats against his life. The relocation follows his role in leading an economic pressure campaign against Iran. U.S. officials concluded the threat warranted the move. The change underscores heightened security concerns for senior officials involved in Iran policy.

news.headline: White House counsel warns incoming House Oversight chair that investigations could breach law
news.summary: White House counsel Will Scharf sent a letter to Rep. Robert Garcia, the incoming Democratic chair of the House Oversight Committee, warning that some planned investigations into the Trump administration might cross legal boundaries. The warning came as Democrats prepared to begin oversight inquiries after regaining control of Congress. The administration framed the warning as a concern over potential criminality, while Democrats said it was an attempt to intimidate. The exchange raises questions about the limits of congressional oversight and executive pushback.

news.headline: Defense Secretary Hegseth reprimanded after group laughs at Tomb of Unknown Soldier
news.summary: During a Veterans Day ceremony at Arlington National Cemetery, an Army sentinel told Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and his senior staff to be silent after laughter was heard near the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. The guard reminded the group to maintain decorum and respect for the memorial. The Pentagon confirmed the incident, noting the sentinel's admonishment. The episode has drawn attention to proper conduct at national memorials.

news.headline: Federal judge allows Donald Trump's $10 bn defamation suit against BBC to proceed
news.summary: A U.S. District Judge in Florida denied the BBC's motion to dismiss part of President Donald Trump's $10 billion defamation lawsuit, allowing the case to move forward. The judge found the complaint plausibly alleges actual malice in the broadcaster's editing of Trump's remarks. The ruling does not decide liability and leaves the lawsuit pending. The case is part of Trump's broader legal actions against media outlets he claims misrepresent him.

news.headline: Democratic senators Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin refuse to back Chuck Schumer for Senate leader
news.summary: Senators Bernie Sanders and Elissa Slotkin announced they will not support Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer for the upcoming Democratic majority leader role. Their statements came after the party's gains in the 2026 midterm elections. The refusals highlight internal debate within Senate Democrats about future leadership. The outcome could affect the party's strategy in the new Congress.

news.headline: Russian Ambassador to U.S., Alexander Darchiev, dies suddenly at 66
news.summary: Russia's Foreign Ministry announced that Ambassador Alexander Darchiev died suddenly on Nov. 11 at age 66. The statement provided no cause of death and described him as an experienced diplomat. Darchiev had served as ambassador since March 2025 and was known for his outspoken criticism of the West. The death raises questions about the future of U.S.-Russia diplomatic relations.

Taco Bell Employee Fired For Passing Drug Test
satire.summary: ANAHEIM, CA — What had looked to be a promising career in the food service industry was abruptly cut short on Wednesday, as a local Taco Bell employee was fired for passing his drug test.

satire.headline: Man Who Says He's Ready For Civil War Needs Wife's Permission To Go Golfing
satire.summary: BLOOMINGTON, MN — Local man Max Carter announced he is 100% ready for a civil war even though he needs his wife's permission to go golfing.
